summary: node1 now serves the approved boot tree as a persistent, read-only TFTP root to node2. Downloads are byte-identical, uploads and traversal are rejected, security controls remain enforced, and both nodes recovered successfully from individual restarts.
actions_performed: Installed the signed RHEL 10 tftp-server 5.2-50.el10 package without upgrading the OS or kernel.
Published only /srv/legacy2/tftp-firmware-distribution/boot using secure chroot mode and systemd read-only protections.
Applied persistent SELinux TFTP labels and constrained transfer ports to UDP 20000–20031.
Restricted node1 TFTP access to node2 and node2 data-port acceptance to node1’s constrained range.
Removed verification artifacts and reviewed final listeners and security state.

evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0; node1’s only package transaction installed tftp-server.

evidence.requirement: Read-only TFTP root and constrained service exposure
evidence.summary: Shows secure boot-root configuration, systemd read-only hardening, persistent SELinux configuration, enabled socket, and source-restricted firewall rules.

evidence.requirement: node2 downloads boot.cfg and firmware.bin with preserved bytes
evidence.summary: Initial source, downloaded, post-restart downloaded, and final source SHA-256 hashes match exactly.
Existing-file overwrite, new-file creation, and parent-directory traversal all fail; approved files remain unchanged and no unauthorized file exists.
Healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, restored service/security/data state, and successful end-to-end client behavior are demonstrated.
Healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, persistent firewall state, successful downloads, and continued rejection behavior are demonstrated.
No task-created temporary residue remains; node1 has the intended TFTP listener and node2 has no TFTP server listener.
